players.note: Jacob Rodriguez showed out in Week 4, notching nine solos and nine assists. Rodriguez has forced his way into the LB1 mix with his stellar IDP production and should be counted as an LB1 option going forward. The LB5 through for weeks of action, Rodriguez is a must-start regardless of opponent.

Jack Campbell showed up in Week 4, reeling off six solos and eight assists. Campbell has been more inconsistent than anyone may have anticipated after his LB1-level run over the past couple of seasons, but having a competent running mate has lowered his weekly floor and, so far, his upside. Campbell is still a top-15 play, but his days of being locked in as a top-three weekly option are over, at least for now. Start Campbell as an upside top-12 option for Week 5.

Ernest Jones was excellent in Week 4, reeling off six solos, six assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one interception, and one pass defended. Jones is locked in as a top-10 option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Jordyn Brooks showed up in Week 4, tallying five solos, eight assists, and one pass defended. Brooks has registered five solos in two of his four contests but looks to have lost the LB1 overall upside he showed in previous seasons with the Dolphins. Teammate Jacob Rodriguez has sapped some of his upside, but he remains a top-12 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Alex Singleton was at it again in Week 4, tallying seven solos, seven assists, and one tackle for loss. Singleton has recorded five or more solos in every game so far, pushing himself back into the LB1 mix in the process. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Foyesade Oluokun showed up in Week 4, racking up six solos, one assist, one forced fumble, one interception, and one pass defended. Oluokun is no longer the top-five mainstay he used to be, but outings like this remind us that the upside is still there. Tap Foye as a top-15 option for Week 5, thanks to a plus matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Tremaine Edmunds showed out in Week 4, racking up eight solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Edmunds looks to be rounding back into his former LB1 form, registering six or more solos in three of four. Edmunds can be counted as a top-15 option going forward.

Arvell Reese has been an elite IDP producer to start his NFL career, most recently tallying nine solos, one tackle for loss, one interception, and three passes defended. Reese has recorded five or more solos in three of his four contests and, thanks to back-to-back splash weeks, is the LB6. Tap Reese as an LB1 play as long as he is cooking.

Jihaad Campbell was excellent in Week 4, racking up nine solos. Jihaad has recorded five or more solos in three of his four contests, helping push him to LB11 status through four weeks of action. Tap Campbell as an LB1 option going forward, including this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Robert Spillane showed up in Week 4, tallying five solos, three assists, and one forced fumble. Spillane has recorded five or more solos in two of four games and remains locked in as a top-15 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Jamien Sherwood was excellent in Week 4, racking up five solos, eight assists, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. This was Sherwood's first game with five or more solos and is hopefully a sign that he is ready to move back towards being the top-15 option IDP managers hoped for. Tap Jamien as a top-25 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Demario Davis was excellent in Week 4, racking up five solos, five assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Demario has been producing at a high level and checks into Week 5 as the LB13 in total fantasy points. Treat the veteran linebacker as a top-25 option while he's cooking.

Josiah Trotter was at it again in Week 4, racking up seven solos and two assists. Trotter has been on fire to start his NFL career, checking into Week 5 as the LB13, thanks to two spike weeks and a splash week in his three games played. Trotter is the LB2 in fppg and should be counted as a top-10 option going forward. Tap Josiah as an LB1 play for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Barrett Carter showed up in Week 4, tallying five solos, six assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Barrett has been a strong LB3 play, recording two games with five solos, while managing just two solos in his other two contests. The inconsistency keeps him in the LB3 realm, but he can be counted among the elites of that tier. Tap Carter as a top-30 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Akeem Davis-Gaither was excellent in Week 4, racking up five solos and three assists. ADG has recorded five or more solos in three of his four games, solidifying the Colts linebacker as a top-20 option going forward. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Payton Wilson stayed hot in Week 4, racking up seven solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Wilson has been a consistent producer on the young season, turning in three spike weeks en route to LB17 status through four games. Wilson is safe to be counted as a top-20 option until he cools down, but the smart money is on Payton staying in the top-25 mix all season.

Devin Bush showed up in Week 4, registering two solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Bush has recorded three or fewer solos in every game this season but has managed to add a tackle for loss in three straight, keeping his fantasy value afloat. Tap Bush as a top-36 option during the byes.

Drake Thomas stayed hot in Week 4, tallying four solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, one interception, and one pass defended. The LB10 through four weeks of action, Drake can be counted as a top-15 option going forward. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Mack Wilson stepped up in Week 4, reeling off four solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Wilson has been the LB3/LB4 type most expected him to be, but has added value now that the byes are here and he just turned in his best fantasy performance of the season. Wilson should have a busy afternoon against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, giving him what should be a solid floor for the plus matchup. Tap Wilson as a top-36 option against Detroit.

T.J. Watt was at it again in Week 4, tallying four solos, one sack, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended. Watt is back to producing at a high level now that he is healthy, and he ranks third in the league with 4.5 sacks, behind only Greg Rousseau and Will Anderson. Watt has worked his way back into the weekly top-three conversation and should be treated as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Dre Greenlaw stepped up in Week 4, racking up seven solos, five assists, and one forced fumble. Greenlaw has disappointed IDP managers since returning to San Francisco, producing like more of a LB3/4 than the LB2 many had him pegged to be. His Week 4 performance was a step in the right direction, especially with the byes finally upon us. Tap Greenlaw as an upside LB3 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Jake Hansen was forced to step up in Week 4 and responded with seven solos, five assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 100 percent of the snaps. Hansen has been thrust into an expanded role since Azeez Al-Shaair suffered a groin injury in Week 3. Hansen should remain a starter after outplaying Kenneth Murray, who may miss Week 5 due to being in concussion protocol. The upside here is viewed as limited, but the spike week puts him in the mix for the byes where the options may get thin. Tap Hansen as a LB3/4 option for a tasty Week 5 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Dorian Williams showed up in Week 4, tallying four solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Williams has recorded four or more solos in every game, settling him as a top-25 option. Count him as one for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Trenton Simpson stepped up in Week 4, tallying two solos, seven assists, one interception, and one pass defended on 56 percent of the snaps. Simpson plays what looks like a rotational role due to Baltimore making frequent use of three safety sets. Teddye Buchanan has seen his role start to grow (19 percent of the snaps in Week 4), but Simpson is going to remain the starter as long as he keeps playing well. The LB15 through four weeks of action, Simpson needs to be rostered and started in all competitive leagues as long as he is cooking.

Byron Young went off in Week 4, racking up four solos, two assists, 2.5 sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Young has settled into life without Jared Verse, Aaron Donald, or Myles Garrett and has recorded at least one sack in two of his last three games. Up to 3.5 sacks on the season, Young will be on sack watch again for Week 5, thanks to a plus matchup against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. Tap Young as a top-five option for the plus matchup.

Dallas Turner stayed hot in Week 4, generating three solos, two sacks, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Turner has recorded at least a half sack in every game this season and is up to 5.5 sacks on the season, good for second in the league. The breakout is real, and it looks like Turner is ready to compete for DPoY honors now that he has a full time role. Treat the Vikings star pass rusher as a top-five option until he cools down considerably.

Omar Speights showed up again in Week 4, racking up five solos and one sack on just 28 percent of the snaps. Speights saw his role dwindle against the Eagles after Saquon Barkley was lost for the game, reducing the need for the Rams to have Omar on the field, since he is usually on the field to stop the run. With that said, Speights has a sack in two straight games and becomes a bye week flex option due to his recent production. You should not want to start him in 12 team leagues, but he has been producing enough to be worth not only rostering but starting for Week 5, thanks to what should be a heavy dose of the run in Week 5 against Josh Allen, James Cook, and the Buffalo Bills.

Khalil Mack was at it again in Week 4, tallying four solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 68 percent of the snaps. Mack now has a sack in three straight games and sits at three on the season. He doesn't appear to need to worry about ceding his snap share to Akheem Mesidor, as Mack, Mesidor, and Tuli Tuipulotu are able to share the field together with Mesidor kicking inside. Mack needs to be treated as a top-25 option as long as he is producing like a DL1.

Darius Robinson showed up in Week 4, notching two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 31 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Darius, who will remain a boom-or-bust DL4/5 type until he shows more consistency or earns a larger weekly snap share. Look elsewhere for your Week 5 DL3.

Harold Perkins stepped up on Monday Night Football, racking up seven solos, three assists, 0.5 sacks, and one pass defended. The rookie sixth-round pick has played over 65 percent of the snaps for two weeks in a row and responded with his first spike week against New Orleans. Perkins has seen his role expand to starter snap territory; that, coupled with his production, has put him on the LB3 radar for Week 5. Treat him as one for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Boye Mafe stepped up in Week 4, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and three tackles for loss. Mafe is leading the Bengals edge group in snaps and should be locked into a starter's role for the rest of the season. He has two sacks on the year and profiles as a boom-or-bust DL3 option. Mafe has DL2 sack upside but is not typically registering enough tackles to keep his value afloat when he doesn't get to the quarterback. Tap Mafe as a top-36 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Odafe Oweh showed up in Week 4, notching one solo, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery on 57 percent of the snaps. Oweh is up to two sacks on the season, but it is in a deep enough rotation that he is going to be more of a boom-or-bust proposition than originally anticipated. He can still be counted as a top-25 option, but expectations should be tempered as far as his weekly floor is concerned. Odafe still has double-digit sack upside, making him a top-25 option going forward.

Josh Uche stepped up in Week 4, tallying two solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. It was the first sack of the season for the Dolphins pass rusher, who played every snap in Week 4, compared to around 50-55 percent in the first three weeks of the season. Uche will have more opportunities to produce if he keeps a starter-level snap share, something that could propel him into the weekly DL3 conversation. For now, keep him glued to benches until he shows more consistency, or we get confirmation that his weekly role has expanded permanently. Look elsewhere for Week 5.

Elijah Ponder was at it again in Week 4, reeling off three solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. Ponder is up to 2.5 sacks on the season, with at least a half sack in three straight games. Harold Landy is at least a few more weeks from returning, giving fantasy managers a strong DL3 option to tap during the early byes. The DL5 through four weeks of action, Ponder needs to be rostered and started everywhere until he cools down.

Zaven Collins stepped up in Week 4, generating three solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. The sack was the first of the season for Collins, who has also started to make more of an impact against the run. He still doesn't play enough snaps to be fantasy relevant most weeks, managing just a 63 percent snap share in Week 4 due to a deep edge rotation in the desert. Stash him in 16+ team leagues, but look elsewhere until he starts to heat up.

Uchenna Nwosu stepped up in Week 4, notching his first sack of the season and finishing with two solos, one assist, the sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Nwosu has two spike weeks to his name, making him bench worthy, but with just one sack and a rotational role that has kept him under 52 percent of the snaps all season, he is hard to trust with just two teams on bye. Keep him stashed where needed, but look elsewhere for your Week 5 DL3.
